messages:
Nina: hitting a parity gap between REST and our Python SDK when onboarding partners. Small but causes routing + telemetry differences.
Oliver: TL;DR?
Nina: REST accepts `route_hint` and preserves it to the routing layer. The Python SDK client `client.chat.create()` doesn't send `route_hint` unless you wrap it inside `meta: {}`. Our sample app passes top-level `route_hint`.
Jamal: so SDK expects a different envelope than REST? That's frustrating.
Nina: yeah. In local repro: curl -> server sees route_hint="priority_pool". SDK -> server sees no route_hint and defaults.
Oliver: is this an intentional API contract change or accidental param drift?
Nina: accidental. The SDK serialization layer maps known fields but there was a refactor that moved `route_hint` into `meta` in the typed client. The REST path still reads top-level.
Jamal: two problems: 1) routing misbehavior (latency + billing), 2) onboarding docs show examples with top-level `route_hint`, so new customers copy sample app and get incorrect behavior.
sdk-ci: [automation] failing test: onboarding/sample-router expecting route_hint to be honored (job 9931)
Oliver: quick mitigation options: a) patch SDK to accept both top-level and `meta.route_hint` (backwards compat), b) change docs to use `meta.route_hint` (breaking for existing sample apps), c) update server to read both locations (works but server-side change is bigger).
Nina: my vote: SDK accept both for now + docs update to show canonical placement. Also emit a deprecation telemetry event when top-level `route_hint` is used.
Jamal: agree. Also flag security: `route_hint` is safe but we must ensure we don't auto-forward arbitrary top-level keys. Add whitelist.
security-bot: [automation] Please file a security review for any metadata-whitelisting changes.
Oliver: another parity quirk: the Python SDK strips `X-Client-Context` header and replaces with `X-Client-Context: sdk-python/0.9.2` losing app-specific context that REST preserves. Some partners rely on that header to stitch logs.
Nina: oh, missed that. If we override without merging, we break observability.
Jamal: plan: 1) hotfix: SDK maps top-level `route_hint` to `meta.route_hint` when sending, preserves any existing `meta`, 2) patch header handling to merge `X-Client-Context` values instead of overwriting, 3) docs: show canonical placement and note legacy top-level usage will be deprecated, 4) add parity tests comparing curl vs SDK for routing header + metadata.
Oliver: timeline?
Nina: hotfix PR today for mapping + header merge. I'll add a unit test that inspects raw request body via httptest. Jamal can handle telemetry + docs update.
Jamal: will open docs PR after unit tests pass. Also adding a nightly parity job to run curl vs SDK on a few endpoints (chat, rerank, embeddings) and diff critical fields.
Oliver: logging: add a small debug log when mapping top-level keys so we can triage customer issues.
security-bot: [automation] Ticket RDW-1422 created for security review of metadata-whitelist and telemetry.
Nina: CI failing on sample onboarding e2e because of routing drift. I pushed a branch with failing test details in the ticket.
sdk-ci: [automation] job 9931 re-run queued after PR build.
Jamal: also capture streaming parity: someone reported SDK coalesces SSE chunks and REST streams token fragments. That affects typing indicators in the sample UI. Add it to the parity checklist.
Oliver: agree. We'll split into two PRs: 1) metadata + headers hotfix, 2) streaming chunking behavior fix. Keep this thread open until e2e passes.
Nina: thanks team. I'll link PR and ticket here once up.
